newsitem.title: UK: Cash Brent mixed, North Sea offshore grades firmer.
newsitem.headline: Cash Brent mixed, North Sea offshore grades firmer.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude paper was mixed early on Monday but offshore loading grades were firmer as buyers looked for protection against rising freight rates, traders said.
July Brent shed 13 cents to $20.22 a barrel by 1222 GMT, slipping back as dealers took profits after Friday's strong rally to two-month highs.
Intermonth spreads were steady to firmer, with June/July talked at +1/+3 cents after trade on Friday at +1 cent.
But North Sea crudes loading offshore and sold on a delivered basis were benefitting from surging tanker rates.
Two cargoes of Norwegian Statfjord loading in the first 10 days of June were sold to a major oil company for Dated Brent +33 cents a barrel, five to seven cents firmer than recent talk.
Tanker rates in northwest Europe jumped by 50 percent last week because of a dearth of tonnage for later this month and some traders said freight could become even more expensive.
Dated Brent was pegged around July Brent -30/-20 cents. The seller of an end-month cargo was hoping to improve on Friday's trade at July Brent -29 cents to a Wall Street trader.
An attractive arbitrage to the U.S. was being balanced by a further deterioration in refining margins, traders said.
Three June 3-5 Brent cargoes were due to turn wet on Monday but traders said one of two cargoes clocked on Friday could be deferred.
In the Mediterranean traders said no deals were reported but at least four end May and one early June Urals cargoes were on offer, with the prompter barrels talked softer than last week.
Traders said the Russian sour crude was talked around Dated Brent -$1.10/-$1.05, but some said prompt cargoes could probably be picked up for as low as Dated Brent -$1.15 or -$1.20.
